contexts.text: He supposes that... everything is connate with him...
A mere external pride is born with some.
Good is born with man, but not truth.
(No man is of the Church from connate good.)
Hence their connate knowledges and affections, as with bees.
As is evident from the inclination or connate nature of both husband and wife...
By virtue of the reaction connate with man...
The good of falsity is not good, but is either pharisaic, meritorious, or connate natural good.
Connate knowledges and affections limit this progression; but connate capacity and inclination limit nothing...
Likenesses and unlikenesses originate from connate inclinations...
From connate timidity; but I added, from connate modesty.
That man has no connate ideas is evident from...
He is then led away from concupiscences... and from the connate avidities for them.
Would they not from connate ferocity...
